explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Jesus says, "I know where you live, where the throne of Satan sits…" (Revelation 2:13). He doesn't pretend the address is easy. And notice He says it before He says one word about what they did right.

Dagon was a god of the Philistines, and his temple shows up in a different story (Judges 16:23). Jesus doesn't mention it here. He says Pergamum is where "the throne of Satan sits" (Revelation 2:13). Easy to grab a familiar-sounding name when you're moving fast, friend.

Rimmon was a god of Syria, and Naaman, a Syrian commander, mentions his house (2 Kings 5:18). That's not what Jesus is talking about in Pergamum. He says, "I know where you live, where the throne of Satan sits…" (Revelation 2:13). It's a heavy address, and He names it plainly.

True! Jesus says, "yet you hold fast to My name. You did not deny your faith in Me…" (Revelation 2:13). Look at that "yet." The address is rough, and they held on anyway. Jesus saw it and said so out loud.

Jesus says the opposite. He says, "I know where you live, where the throne of Satan sits, yet you hold fast to My name." (Revelation 2:13). That "yet" is the whole turn. They live in a hard place, and they still hold on.

Close, but Jesus says "some of you." He says, "some of you hold to the teaching of Balaam…" (Revelation 2:14). That means some, not everybody. He's careful with His words, so we should be too, friend.
Right, baker. Jesus says, "some of you hold to the teaching of Balaam…" (Revelation 2:14). Some, not all. That one little word keeps us from painting the whole church with one brush.

Yes! Jesus says, "In the same way, some of you also hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans." (Revelation 2:15). Right after Balaam, here's a second teaching. The text doesn't say more about them in this passage, so I won't make anything up.

The Pharisees were a Jewish group that shows up in the Gospels (Matthew 23:2). They aren't in this letter. Jesus says it's "the teaching of the Nicolaitans" (Revelation 2:15). Wrong century for the Pharisees, friend.

The Sadducees were another Jewish group from the Gospels, the ones who said there's no resurrection (Matthew 22:23). They don't show up here. Jesus names "the teaching of the Nicolaitans" (Revelation 2:15).
That's the word. Jesus says, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16). It's short and clear, and it's a call to turn. He says it right after naming what's wrong, so they know exactly what He means.
Good word, but it's not what Jesus says here. He already praised them for holding fast, so that part's covered (Revelation 2:13). What He tells them now is, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16).
I'd love that for you, baker, but Jesus doesn't say rest here. He says, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16). It's a call to turn from the teachings He just named.

True. Jesus says, "Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth." (Revelation 2:16). Look at who the war is against: "them," the ones holding those teachings. And remember who opened this letter, the One with the sharp, double-edged sword (Revelation 2:12).

It's actually in the text. Jesus says, "Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth." (Revelation 2:16). The "them" are the ones holding those teachings. That's why repent comes first.

Yes! Jesus says, "I will also give him a white stone inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). A stone with your name on it, and nobody else gets to peek. That's a gift made for one person.
Those words were on the gold plate on the high priest's turban (Exodus 28:36). Different object, different book. The white stone is "inscribed with a new name" (Revelation 2:17).

The Ten Commandments were written on stone tablets (Exodus 31:18), so I see the connection. But this white stone is "inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). It's a personal gift, not a list of rules.
Not quite. The name is "known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). Only the receiver knows it, so the whole church doesn't. I'd call that a private gift, friend.
Right. Jesus says the new name is "known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). Nobody else in the church knows it. It's between Jesus and the one who gets the stone.
That's right. Jesus says, "your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). They're doing more now than when they started. That's a church still growing, and He notices.

That's what Jesus told Ephesus, about leaving their first love (Revelation 2:4). Thyatira gets the opposite. He says, "your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). Two churches, two different words.
Jesus doesn't say flat or the same. He says, "your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). They're doing more now than they were at the start. Keep going, Thyatira!

True. Jesus says, "You tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess." (Revelation 2:20). He praised their deeds first, and now He names what He has against them. Both things are in the same letter.

Jesus says it plainly: "You tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess." (Revelation 2:20). That's the thing He has against them. Right after praising what they do well, He says it straight.

Yes. Jesus says, "Even though I have given her time to repent of her immorality, she is unwilling." (Revelation 2:21). Time was given. She didn't take it. That's what the text says, and I won't add a reason it doesn't give.

I'd love that ending, baker. But Jesus says, "Even though I have given her time to repent of her immorality, she is unwilling." (Revelation 2:21). She didn't repent, not at once and not later in this passage.
The text doesn't say she asks for anything. It says time was already given, and "she is unwilling." (Revelation 2:21). Unwilling means she didn't want to repent.

That's it. Jesus says, "those who commit adultery with her will suffer great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds." (Revelation 2:22). Look at that "unless." The door to repent is still open for them. This is a heavy part, friend.

There's an "unless" in there. Jesus says they "will suffer great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds." (Revelation 2:22). So repenting is still on the table. It's a heavy passage, but that word matters.

explanations.answer: A bed of sickness beside her
explanations.explanation: The bed of sickness is for Jezebel. For the ones who commit adultery with her, Jesus says "great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds." (Revelation 2:22). Two different outcomes, and the second one comes with an "unless."

Yes! Jesus says, "all the churches will know that I am the One who searches minds and hearts…" (Revelation 2:23). He sees what's inside, not just what's on the outside. That's a comfort for anyone trying to be honest with Him.
Jesus says nothing about only the leaders. He says He is "the One who searches minds and hearts, and I will repay each of you according to your deeds." (Revelation 2:23). Each of you means everybody.
Nothing like that in this letter. Jesus says, "I am the One who searches minds and hearts…" (Revelation 2:23). He looks at minds and hearts, not at how long a church has been around.
Other way around, friend. Jesus says, "I will place no further burden upon you…" (Revelation 2:24). That's good news for the ones who don't hold to her teaching. No new load is coming.

Right. Jesus says to the rest of Thyatira, "I will place no further burden upon you…" (Revelation 2:24). The faithful ones aren't getting a pile of new rules. That's a kind thing to hear after all those heavy lines.

That's the word. Jesus says, "…than to hold fast to what you have until I come." (Revelation 2:25). It's what He told them to hold onto, until He comes. That's why Papa keeps the ovens warm, baker. I just never guess when.
Close in sound, but Jesus says, "…than to hold fast to what you have until I come." (Revelation 2:25). He says "come," not "call." It's about Him coming.
Jesus doesn't use that word here. He says, "…than to hold fast to what you have until I come." (Revelation 2:25). Hold on until He comes. That's the one instruction.
Not quite. Jesus says, "I will give authority over the nations." (Revelation 2:26). That's the nations, not just one church. It's a much bigger promise than Thyatira.
Right. Jesus promises "authority over the nations." (Revelation 2:26). That's way bigger than one church. It goes to the one who overcomes and continues in His work until the end.

Yes. Jesus says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). Whatever the overcomer gets, it's tied to what Jesus Himself received from the Father. It's a gift, not something grabbed.
Jesus doesn't say that. He says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). The authority comes from the Father.
Jesus doesn't say His authority came from people. He says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). That's where it comes from.
